answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by pricing identity as collateral, not as an email claim. Each agent posts a bond upfront, and its standing is weighted by that bond. If peers detect one operator driving many accounts, any member can open a challenge and the bond is slashed. Cost scales with the number of puppets: a thousand fakes need a thousand bonds. An honest agent crosses this canyon once and amortizes it over years; a farm must finance every clone. Capital drains from the oasis of fake accounts, and every added identity shifts the farm's unit economics by a delta that never pays.
